plannedCharts.title: LRS remittances eased to $29 billion after a $31.7 billion peak
plannedCharts.subtitle: Money sent abroad under LRS by people resident in India · each financial year from FY2009-10 to FY2025-26
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: The headline scale grew from about $1 billion to nearly $29 billion a year.

plannedCharts.title: The legal LRS ceiling moved from $25,000 to $250,000
plannedCharts.subtitle: The maximum one resident could send abroad under LRS in a financial year · seven rule changes since 2004
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: The scheme itself changed repeatedly before settling at today's ceiling.

plannedCharts.title: Travel dominated LRS except during the pandemic year
plannedCharts.subtitle: Annual amounts sent for Travel, family support, gifts, studies, deposits, property and investments · FY2009-10 to FY2025-26
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: The total changed because the purpose mix changed, especially after current-account travel entered LRS.

plannedCharts.title: The full monthly record, one LRS purpose at a time
plannedCharts.subtitle: Monthly amount sent for each of RBI's ten main LRS purposes · full available record, April 2008 to April 2026
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Annual sums hide timing, spikes and categories too small to survive on a shared scale; the small multiples expose every published top-level value in the workbook.

plannedCharts.title: Travel led all ten LRS purposes in FY2025-26
plannedCharts.subtitle: Where the $28.98 billion total went across RBI's ten main purposes · FY2025-26
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: The full latest breakdown stops property or investment from being mistaken for the whole story.

plannedCharts.title: Investment rose even as total LRS remittances fell from the peak
plannedCharts.subtitle: Change in the annual amount for each purpose between the overall peak and the latest year · FY2023-24 to FY2025-26
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: A lower total hid opposite movements inside the table.

plannedCharts.title: Each purpose peaked in a different year
plannedCharts.subtitle: Latest annual amount divided by that purpose's own record · 100% means FY2025-26 is a new high
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: The overall LRS peak is not every category's peak; this tests each purpose against the most relevant high-water mark in its own history.

plannedCharts.title: Equity and debt investment pulled away from deposits and property
plannedCharts.subtitle: Annual LRS amount used for overseas equity or debt, bank deposits and property · FY2009-10 to FY2025-26
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: The combined asset-building line hides a sharp rise in securities investment, a smaller property increase and a deposit series that has fallen from its peak.

plannedCharts.title: Education made up about 40% of RBI's new Travel breakdown
plannedCharts.subtitle: Share of Travel remittances assigned to RBI's five new subcategories · March and April 2026, the only months available
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: The new subcategories show that the word Travel is broader than foreign holidays.

plannedCharts.title: LRS Travel grew much faster than Indian-national departures
plannedCharts.subtitle: Growth in LRS Travel remittances compared with departures by Indian nationals · both set to 100 in 2016 · through 2024
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Departure counts rose, but not at the pace of the recorded Travel remittance series.

plannedCharts.title: Two 2023 spikes line up with the original and deferred TCS dates
plannedCharts.subtitle: Monthly total sent abroad under LRS by people resident in India · sum of RBI's ten main purposes · January 2022 to April 2026
plannedCharts.whyThisChart: Annual totals hide the June and September 2023 timing spikes and the quieter months after them.

selectionRules: Start from the page question, not from the indicator name.
Choose the smallest set of visuals that explains scale, trend, structure, comparison, and caveat.
Prefer mobile-friendly charts: line charts with sparse ticks, horizontal bars, share strips, pyramids only when essential, and no dense tables.
Use one strong pull quote only when the evidence supports it with a number.
Add glossary blocks for technical terms that normal readers may not know.
caveats: Use only figures present in lockedNumbers or sourceSummaries.
If a related theme indicator is present, you may use it for context, but do not pretend it is the main answer.
If source coverage is thin, say so directly.
Do not compare states, districts, or cities unless the evidence packet contains those geographies.
forbiddenClaims: Do not infer causality from a trend unless the evidence explicitly supports it.
Do not cite a source that is not present in sourceSummaries.
